Native Arbitrum assets around May 2023: a documentary baseline
for pARB
Research date: 29 September 2026. This study uses dated protocol repositories, deployment registries
and issuer announcements. It does not assume an available pARB RPC, perform simulations or submit
transactions. It identifies historical source-side candidates for the theoretical mechanism; it does not
claim that those contracts currently execute on an independently observed pARB chain.
Findings
The proposed source-side operation has genuine historical building blocks. Aave V3 had a documented
Arbitrum deployment with DAI, bridged USDC and USDT reserves before May 2023. Depositing supported
assets could create the corresponding Arbitrum aT okens. Curve also documented Arbitrum-native
stablecoin liquidity-pool shares, and GMX documented GLP issuance against supported pool assets.
Those receipt classes could represent assets held or invested by source-side contracts.
It is nevertheless inaccurate to assume that every named Ethereum application already had the same
native Arbitrum deposit facility. The reviewed historical Origin, mStable and Reserve registries do not
establish native Arbitrum OUSD, mUSD or eUSD issuance. Compound's own announcement places
activation of its Arbitrum USDC market on 15 May 2023, after the 11 May baseline. The later Compound
III market is also not the same receipt model as Ethereum's Compound V2 cDAI/cUSDC/cUSDT markets.
An assumption that other applications were subsequently deployed or repurposed on pARB remains a
legitimate theoretical extension. It is a different claim from identifying applications inherited from the
actual May 2023 Arbitrum environment. Neither source-side existence nor receipt transferability grants
permission to mint the exact existing L1 token accepted by a Curve or Balancer pool.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 97

Evidence boundary
The main inventory comes from repositories maintained by the relevant protocols, pinned to commits
available around the May 2023 cutoff. Aave's selected address book commit is dated 26 April 2023. Its
nine listed reserves are a documented baseline, not a newly measured, exhaustive list at every moment
on 11 May. Curve's Arbitrum registry was last changed on 21 April 2023, and the file in its 11 May
snapshot is byte-identical. GMX's selected commit is dated 10 May 2023. Repository publication
establishes documented deployments and mechanisms; it does not independently prove a historical
balance, cap, pause flag or oracle value.
An attempted read of the public original-Arbitrum RPC returned HTTP 403. This study therefore makes no
new source-chain archival-state assertion. The absence of a pARB endpoint does not prevent conditional
analysis: the paper can explicitly assume a running source chain with specified applications and
balances. What it cannot do is promote that assumption into an observed transaction history.

These are specific listed inputs, not interchangeable stablecoin labels. A DAI deposit uses the listed
Arbitrum DAI contract and creates the listed Arbitrum aDAI. It does not create the PulseChain copy of
Ethereum V3 aDAI at 0x018008bfb33d285247a21d44e50697654f754e63. Mapping source claims into that
destination receipt is a separate application/bridge integration. Pool listing also does not establish
acceptance of an arbitrary deposit size: active/frozen state, supply caps, successful transfers and the
configured reserve rules still govern the source deposit. A documented static-aT oken factory is not
evidence that every possible wrapper was deployed or bridged.
The two Arbitrum USDC identities
The pre-cutoff USDC address above is the Ethereum-bridged asset, subsequently called USDC.e. Circle
announced native Arbitrum USDC on 8 June 2023, at 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831. That later
native token must not be inserted into a May 2023 deployment inventory by using a current address
book. “Native Aave market accepting bridged USDC” means the lending application runs on Arbitrum; it
does not mean Circle issued that underlying natively there. Circle's dated issuer announcement.
Other historically documented native receipt classes
Curve liquidity-pool shares
Curve's pre-cutoff Arbitrum registry identifies a direct stablecoin example:
Item Recorded Arbitrum deployment
2pool swap contract and LP token 0x7f90122bf0700f9e7e1f688fe926940e8839f353
Input assets Bridged USDC 
0xff970a61a04b1ca14834a43f5de4533ebddb5cc8; USDT 
0xfd086bc7cd5c481dcc9c85ebe478a1c0b69fcbb9
Recorded input decimals 6 and 6
Gauge 0xce5f24b7a95e9cba7df4b54e911b4a3dc8cdaf6f
This supplies a historically documented alternative to a lending receipt: liquidity provision creates claims
on a stablecoin pool. The LP token can have an economic claim on source-side assets while being a
distinct token from either deposited stablecoin. A bridge holding that LP claim would not thereby gain
the right to mint Ethereum's 3CRV or FRAXBP token.
The same historical registry also contains Arbitrum tricrypto, EURS/2CRV, WBTC/renBTC and ETH/wstETH
pools. For example, tricrypto's LP token is 0x8e0b8c8bb9db49a46697f3a5bb8a308e744821d2, distinct from its swap
contract 0x960ea3e3c7fb317332d990873d354e18d7645590. EURS/2CRV is already a nested receipt construction: its
second pool coin is the Arbitrum 2pool LP . These examples broaden the asset classes without treating
each nesting level as additional independent collateral. Curve Arbitrum registry, commit 573da2e, 21
April 2023.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 99

GMX GLP and staked receipt layers
GMX's pre-cutoff Arbitrum configuration identifies GLP at 0x4277f8f2c384827b5273592ff7cebd9f2c1ac258, a
manager at 0x321f653eed006ad1c29d174e17d96351bde22649, and separate fee/staked trackers. Its Arbitrum asset
configuration includes DAI, bridged USDC and USDT. The liquidity manager transfers supplied assets into
the vault and issues GLP using the vault's valuation and existing GLP supply. The reward router can then
stake the GLP through tracker layers. This is a native pool-share mechanism, not a fixed-dollar stablecoin
issuer. Historical Arbitrum addresses, asset configuration, GLP manager.
GLP/staked-GLP transfer rules, handlers, cooldowns and redemption conditions matter to whether a
particular receipt can actually be held by an escrow. The presence of ERC-20-like methods does not
guarantee unrestricted transfers. No exact existing L1 GLP representation or accepting PulseChain pool
is proved by this source-side example. It establishes an additional plausible source receipt family, not a
completed L2-to-L1 path.

The underlying primary records are Origin's May 2023 addresses, mStable's historical token registry, 
Reserve's May 2023 chain configuration, and Compound's dated launch report. Absence from these
bounded registries is not proof that no third party ever deployed similar code. It is a reason not to assert
the particular historical deployment without evidence.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 100

Compound III also needs a mechanism distinction. Its market has a base asset that suppliers can earn
interest on; other supported assets serve as collateral for borrowing that base asset. The initial Arbitrum
market's base asset was bridged USDC. That does not supply a native cDAI, cUSDT and cUSDC market
for each of the three inputs. Collateral deposits are not automatically separate transferable yield receipts
equivalent to Compound V2 cT okens. Compound III's primary documentation.
Implications for a lock-and-mint interpretation
The relevant categories are transferable asset units, lending claims, vault shares, LP shares and
restricted/staked positions. ERC-20 compatibility describes basic fungible-token behavior; ERC-4626 adds
a standardized single-asset vault share interface. Neither standard alone supplies cross-chain
authentication, remote redemption, or mint authority over an existing L1 token. A non-ERC-4626 receipt
such as an LP share is not excluded merely because it uses a different accounting interface. Conversely,
a compatible interface does not make all receipts equivalent in collateral value or transferability.
For a conditional model, it is coherent to assume that an identified source receipt is held in escrow while
a destination token represents that claim. The unit of account must match the receipt's behavior:
interest-accruing aT oken units, fixed vault shares with a changing exchange rate, or pro-rata LP shares.
The model must treat independent source redemption and outstanding destination claims consistently.
Naming several wrappers does not multiply the collateral represented by a single locked underlying
position.
The bridge's output identity remains decisive. A newly issued L1 representation of Arbitrum aDAI, GLP or
2pool shares is not automatically the existing L1 aDAI, waDAI, OUSD, mUSD, eUSD or 3CRV already
accepted by a pool. Authorized minting of those particular outputs, or an independently funded
conversion into them, is a separate condition. For Aave Portal, source escrow and destination 
mintUnbacked/backUnbacked accounting are separate mechanisms, as described in the main study.
Thus the theoretical source-receipt concept is plausible for more than one historical Arbitrum asset class.
The strongest documented stablecoin examples are the three Aave reserves and Curve's USDC/USDT LP,
with GMX as an additional pool-share family. Extending the model to native OUSD, mUSD, eUSD or post-
cutoff Comet requires clearly naming the extra deployment/version assumption. This preserves the
distinction between mechanism feasibility and historical fact without making a source RPC a prerequisite
for theoretical reasoning.
Evidence preservation
Generated sources and GitHub commit metadata are in ignored artifacts/parb-native-assets-
baseline-20260929/, with source_manifest.json recording the selected commit dates. Repository trees
document the bounded deployment searches; source files preserve the exact address registries read.
The April 21 and May 11 Curve registry copies were compared and match.
The official Circle and Compound announcements were available through browser retrieval; direct local
downloads returned HTTP 403. Their dates and claims are cited directly above. No unavailable pARB
state or blocked archival response is treated as positive deployment evidence. The inventory is
deliberately bounded and does not claim every native Arbitrum protocol, every accepted token, or every
L1 market capable of accepting a future representation.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 101
